lines.text: You sit up in bed. You are not sure why.
The clock radio says 1:59. It has said 1:59 for a while now.

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: Huh.
Your flashlight is in your pajama pocket. {menu} turns it on and off.
You sit up in bed. 1:59 again.

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: Same time tomorrow. Right.
1:59. The little dots between the numbers are not even blinking.
Still 1:59. You could have a staring contest with it. It would win.
Your desk. Homework you finished. Homework you said you finished.

bedroom_drawing.todo: TODO(Tadzio): who is in the drawing? Does tearing it down (drawing_torn) change anything later?

lines.text: A drawing you made and taped to the wall.
It's somebody you used to like. You drew them smiling.
Rrrrip. The tape keeps a strip of it.
Tape, and a strip of paper. You don't remember the rest.
The street is dark. One lamp is on, far away.
Under it, something small and bright moves around. Then it stops. Like it's thinking.
Clothes. Shoes. No monsters. You checked at bedtime.
Not yet.
Books, a good rock, a cup with three pencils. Nothing is out of place. That is the weird part.
A glass of water. Half full, if anybody asks.
The plant is asleep. Plants are good at that.
Dad's door is closed.
He sleeps like a log. A log would be louder.
The bathroom. The light is off. It is staying off. Probably.
Across the street, every window is dark. Every single one.
The bathroom light flickers. Once.

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: ...Okay.
The fridge is humming.
It knows a song. You have never heard the fridge know a song.
You hum along. The fridge stops.
Then it starts again. A little louder. A little proud.
The stove is off. You check twice anyway.
Drip. ... ... Drip. Slower than usual.
The backyard. Out past the gate, something bright bobs by and is gone.
Your cereal bowl is already out for the morning. Somebody plans ahead.
The back door is unlocked.
It is never unlocked.
Cold.
The grass is wet. Your slippers were not built for this.
A small light bobs past the gate.

lines.speaker: tadzio
lines.text: Hey-
It's gone. It went toward the street.
Garden stuff. A trowel, a glove, the other glove.
The family notice board. One note says: FEED THE DUMMY? (IT IS A DUMMY.) Another just says: GLOVE.
The kitchen window. From out here, your house looks like someone else's.
Somewhere in town, a clock chimes. Two.
